section: Governor - appointment, powers, discretionary powers, position and controversies (Article 200/201, Article 356 reports)
subsections: Reservation of bills for President - Articles 200/201, mandatory cases, time limits (TN Governor case)

accepted.s: Under Article 200 of the Constitution, which one of the following is NOT an option available to the Governor in respect of a Bill passed by the State Legislature?
o: To withhold assent to the Bill
To assent to the Bill
To reserve the Bill for the consideration of the President
To return a Money Bill for reconsideration
accepted.x: The Governor may return a Bill for reconsideration only if it is not a Money Bill. The other three are options available under Article 200.
accepted.tq: Identify the exception by applying the special constitutional rule for Money Bills.
accepted.sec: Reservation of bills for President - Articles 200/201, mandatory cases, time limits (TN Governor case)  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Governor's power under Article 200:
1. The Governor may assent to a Bill passed by the State Legislature.
2. The Governor may withhold assent to a Bill.
3. The Governor may reserve a Bill for the consideration of the President.
4. The Governor may return a Money Bill for reconsideration.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
o: 1, 2 and 3 only
1 and 4 only
2, 3 and 4 only
accepted.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct options under Article 200. Statement 4 is false because a Money Bill cannot be returned for reconsideration by the Governor.
accepted.tq: Split the options by checking the constitutional exception relating to Money Bills.
accepted.sec: Reservation of bills for President - Articles 200/201, mandatory cases, time limits (TN Governor case)  [APPSC]

accepted.s: When a Bill returned by the Governor is passed again by the State Legislature, which one of the following is constitutionally correct?
o: The Governor must assent to the Bill and cannot withhold assent again.
The Bill automatically becomes law without any further action.
The Bill must necessarily be reserved for the President.
The Governor may withhold assent again at his discretion.
accepted.x: If the Legislature re-passes a Bill that was returned for reconsideration, the Governor must assent to it and cannot withhold assent again.
accepted.tq: Test the effect of re-passage rather than the Governor's initial alternatives.
accepted.sec: Reservation of bills for President - Articles 200/201, mandatory cases, time limits (TN Governor case)  [APPSC]

accepted.s: A Bill once reserved for the consideration of the President may be reserved again after re-enactment only when it has been:
o: Materially altered
Passed by a two-thirds majority
Approved by the State Cabinet unanimously
Certified as a Money Bill
accepted.x: A Bill may be reserved only once. A re-enacted Bill cannot ordinarily be reserved again unless it has been materially altered.
accepted.tq: Use the qualifying condition to distinguish a general rule from its exception.
accepted.sec: Reservation of bills for President - Articles 200/201, mandatory cases, time limits (TN Governor case)  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following Bills must be reserved by the Governor for the consideration of the President?
o: Every Bill passed by the Legislative Council
A Bill that derogates from the powers of the High Court
Every Bill relating to State taxation
Every Bill concerning local self-government
accepted.x: Reservation is mandatory where a Bill derogates from the powers of the High Court. The other categories do not require reservation merely for the reasons stated.
accepted.tq: Apply the mandatory-case rule and reject broad overstatements using “every”.
accepted.sec: Reservation of bills for President - Articles 200/201, mandatory cases, time limits (TN Governor case)  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. A Bill derogating from the powers of the High Court is a case of mandatory reservation by the Governor.
2. Reservation of every Bill affecting State finances is mandatory.
3. Reservation may operate as a form of central control over the States.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
o: 1 only
1 and 3 only
2 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
accepted.x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is false because every Bill affecting State finances need not be mandatorily reserved.
accepted.tq: Find the overbroad statement while retaining the precise constitutional propositions.
accepted.sec: Reservation of bills for President - Articles 200/201, mandatory cases, time limits (TN Governor case)  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Reservation of a State Bill for the President's consideration is constitutionally associated with which one of the following broader consequences?
o: It transfers the Bill automatically to the Supreme Court.
It makes the Governor the final authority over the Bill.
It is a form of central control over the States.
It eliminates the legislative competence of the State Legislature permanently.
accepted.x: Reservation gives the Union executive, through the President, a role in the final consideration of the State Bill and is therefore treated as a form of central control over States.
accepted.tq: Apply the federal-structure implication of the constitutional power.
accepted.sec: Reservation of bills for President - Articles 200/201, mandatory cases, time limits (TN Governor case)  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Which of the following pairs are correctly matched?
1. Compulsory acquisition of property — Articles 31A/31C
2. Repugnancy of a Concurrent List Bill — Article 254(2)
3. Taxation on water or electricity in certain inter-State river projects — Article 288
4. Restrictions on inter-State trade — Article 304(b)
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
o: 1 and 2 only
2 and 3 only
1, 3 and 4 only
accepted.x: All four pairs are correctly associated with constitutional situations in which Presidential protection, sanction or consideration becomes relevant. Article 304(b) concerns restrictions on trade, commerce or intercourse within India.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure Article–subject pairs and verify all four constitutional provisions.
accepted.sec: Reservation of bills for President - Articles 200/201, mandatory cases, time limits (TN Governor case)  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Constitutional provision)
A. Article 200
B. Article 201
C. Article 254(2)
D. Article 360

List-II (Subject)
1. Bills reserved for the President
2. Governor's action on Bills passed by the State Legislature
3. Repugnant State law in the Concurrent List
4. Financial Emergency

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: Article 200 deals with the Governor's choices on a State Bill; Article 201 deals with Bills reserved for the President; Article 254(2) concerns Concurrent List repugnancy; and Article 360 concerns Financial Emergency.
accepted.tq: Start from the Article 200–Governor pair and eliminate codes with misplaced provisions.
accepted.sec: Reservation of bills for President - Articles 200/201, mandatory cases, time limits (TN Governor case)  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Article 201:
1. The President may withhold assent to a Bill reserved by the Governor.
2. In the case of a non-Money Bill, the President may direct the Governor to return it to the State Legislature.
3. The Constitution prescribes a fixed period within which the President must decide every reserved Bill.
4. Even after reconsideration by the Legislature, the President is not bound to assent to the Bill.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
o: 1 and 2 only
1, 2 and 4 only
2, 3 and 4 only
accepted.x: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 3 is false because Article 201 prescribes no fixed time limit for the President's decision on a reserved Bill.
accepted.tq: Use the absence of a prescribed time limit as the discriminating statement.
accepted.sec: Reservation of bills for President - Articles 200/201, mandatory cases, time limits (TN Governor case)  [APPSC]

accepted.s: A State Bill imposing restrictions on inter-State trade under Article 304(b) requires, before its introduction in the State Legislature:
o: The consent of every neighbouring State
The approval of the Inter-State Council
The assent of the Supreme Court
The previous sanction of the President
accepted.x: A Bill imposing reasonable restrictions on trade, commerce or intercourse with or within a State under Article 304(b) requires the previous sanction of the President before introduction.
accepted.tq: Ask which authority gives the prior sanction, a common authority-swapping trap.
accepted.sec: Reservation of bills for President - Articles 200/201, mandatory cases, time limits (TN Governor case)  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Arrange the following developments in chronological order:
A. Opinion of the five-judge Bench in the 16th Presidential Reference
B. Judgment in State of Punjab v. Principal Secretary to Governor
C. Judgment in State of Tamil Nadu v. Governor of Tamil Nadu
D. Presidential Reference under Article 143 was considered in November 2025

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
o: B, C, D, A
B, D, C, A
C, B, D, A
D, B, C, A
accepted.x: The Punjab judgment was delivered in 2023, the Tamil Nadu judgment on 8 April 2025, and the Article 143 Presidential Reference opinion was delivered in November 2025. The opinion itself is the development represented by A, following the Reference represented by D.
accepted.tq: Fix the known dates first and then place the Reference opinion after the Reference process.
accepted.sec: Reservation of bills for President - Articles 200/201, mandatory cases, time limits (TN Governor case)  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Supreme Court's decision in State of Punjab v. Principal Secretary to Governor (2023) held that the Governor:
o: Could reserve every State Bill for the President without giving reasons
Could keep Bills pending indefinitely if no time limit was expressly stated
Must act as soon as possible and cannot keep Bills pending indefinitely
Could reject a Bill permanently after returning it once
accepted.x: The 2023 Punjab case held that the Governor must act as soon as possible and cannot keep Bills pending indefinitely. It also affirmed the consequence of re-passage of a returned Bill.
accepted.tq: Test the operative judicial direction using the precise phrase “as soon as possible”.
accepted.sec: Reservation of bills for President - Articles 200/201, mandatory cases, time limits (TN Governor case)  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following was associated with the judgment in State of Tamil Nadu v. Governor of Tamil Nadu delivered on 8 April 2025?
o: The Court prescribed time periods and used Article 142 to declare ten Bills assented to.
The Court held that the Governor could reserve a Bill repeatedly without alteration.
The Court declared that no constitutional time limits could ever be considered.
The Court abolished the President's power to withhold assent under Article 201.
accepted.x: The April 2025 judgment prescribed timelines of one month, three months and one month in specified situations and used Article 142 to grant deemed assent to ten Bills.
accepted.tq: Separate the April 2025 judgment from the later Presidential Reference that altered its effect.
accepted.sec: Reservation of bills for President - Articles 200/201, mandatory cases, time limits (TN Governor case)  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Which of the following correctly states the timelines read into Article 200 by the April 2025 Tamil Nadu Governor judgment?
1. One month where assent was withheld on the advice of the Council of Ministers.
2. Three months where action was taken against the advice of the Council of Ministers.
3. One month for action on a Bill re-presented after re-passage.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
o: 1 and 2 only
1 and 3 only
2 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
accepted.x: The April 2025 judgment read into Article 200 a one-month period for withholding assent on advice, three months for action against advice, and one month after re-presentation of a re-passed Bill.
accepted.tq: Numerical comparison of three closely related time limits.
accepted.sec: Reservation of bills for President - Articles 200/201, mandatory cases, time limits (TN Governor case)  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The opinion of the five-judge Bench in the 16th Presidential Reference under Article 143, delivered in November 2025, held that:
o: The Governor must always act strictly according to the advice of the State Council of Ministers under Article 200.
Courts may prescribe fixed timelines and grant deemed assent whenever the Governor delays.
The President must obtain the Supreme Court's advice on every Bill reserved under Article 201.
Courts cannot impose timelines or declare deemed assent, though prolonged unexplained inaction may attract a limited direction to decide.
accepted.x: The November 2025 opinion rejected court-imposed timelines and deemed assent. It nevertheless recognised that prolonged unexplained inaction may be addressed through a limited direction to decide.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the current constitutional position from the earlier judicially prescribed timelines.
accepted.sec: Reservation of bills for President - Articles 200/201, mandatory cases, time limits (TN Governor case)  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements in the light of the November 2025 Presidential Reference opinion:
1. Deemed assent was held to be unconstitutional.
2. Judicial review is limited to issues such as mala fides and procedure.
3. Courts may impose a fixed deadline for every Bill pending before a Governor.
4. The President need not seek the Supreme Court's advice on each reserved Bill.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
o: 1 and 2 only
1, 2 and 4 only
2, 3 and 4 only
accepted.x: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 3 is false because the Presidential Reference rejected court-imposed timelines, while permitting limited intervention in cases of prolonged unexplained inaction.
accepted.tq: Reject the extreme statement that converts limited judicial review into a universal power to set deadlines.
accepted.sec: Reservation of bills for President - Articles 200/201, mandatory cases, time limits (TN Governor case)  [APPSC]

accepted.s: According to the November 2025 opinion in the 16th Presidential Reference, the Governor, while choosing among the options under Article 200, is:
o: Required to refer every Bill to the Supreme Court
Bound in every case by the advice of the State Council of Ministers
Not bound by such advice in choosing among the Article 200 options
Required to follow the advice of the President alone
accepted.x: The Presidential Reference opinion stated that the Governor is not bound by the advice of the State Council of Ministers while choosing among the options available under Article 200.
accepted.tq: Test the distinction between constitutional discretion under Article 200 and ordinary aid-and-advice situations.
accepted.sec: Reservation of bills for President - Articles 200/201, mandatory cases, time limits (TN Governor case)  [APPSC]

accepted.s: In the context of the 16th Presidential Reference, the Governor was described as the:
o: Permanent representative of the Union Cabinet in the State
Final constitutional sovereign of the State
Judicial guardian of the State Legislature
Guide, philosopher and friend of the government
accepted.x: The November 2025 Presidential Reference opinion described the Governor as a “guide, philosopher and friend” of the government.
accepted.tq: Direct recall of the distinctive constitutional phrase used in the opinion.
accepted.sec: Reservation of bills for President - Articles 200/201, mandatory cases, time limits (TN Governor case)  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements most accurately reflects the present position after the November 2025 Presidential Reference opinion?
o: A court may automatically treat every delayed Bill as assented to.
The April 2025 timelines continue to apply without qualification in every State.
A Governor may keep a Bill pending indefinitely because Article 200 contains no express deadline.
There can be no court-imposed general timeline or deemed assent, but prolonged unexplained inaction may be subject to a limited judicial direction.
accepted.x: The current position rejects general court-imposed timelines and deemed assent, while allowing limited judicial intervention where inaction is prolonged and unexplained. The April 2025 timelines do not survive as universally enforceable rules.
accepted.tq: Compare the earlier judgment with the later Presidential Reference and identify the surviving principle.
accepted.sec: Reservation of bills for President - Articles 200/201, mandatory cases, time limits (TN Governor case)  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following States were identified as having experienced the longest delays in dealing with Bills by Governors?
o: Kerala and Tamil Nadu
Maharashtra and Karnataka
Punjab and Haryana
Andhra Pradesh and Telangana
accepted.x: Kerala and Tamil Nadu were identified as the States that saw the longest delays in dealing with Bills by Governors.
accepted.tq: Use a paired-place recall question to test the specific comparison rather than a general statement about delay.
accepted.sec: Reservation of bills for President - Articles 200/201, mandatory cases, time limits (TN Governor case)  [APPSC]
